quest.title: Vision of Ashen Desolation
quest.description: In order to help Leyla find his spirit, Citlali plans to get more info from within the tribe, but how successful was she...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Incense Ashcrystals x80, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Ah, Granny. You're back.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So... no good news for me, then?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #You saw right through me. {NICKNAME} collected a lot of spirits, and I checked all of them one by one. None of them matches Leyla's description.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I figured. It was written all over your face. It's alright, I didn't exactly have high hopes for the needle-in-a-haystack approach anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Leyla's condition is still stable, but we're not really getting anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Well, luckily I made some progress on my end. Leyla's parents told me that he made a new friend recently, and apparently, he's been out of the house for days at a time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: On one occasion, they secretly followed him, and saw him and his friend tinkering around with something at a camp.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They saw his friend?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yeah, some guy who goes by the name "Kokuchuu." Dressed in what looked like Inazuman attire.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Is this really all I'll need, Mr. Kokuchuu?

dialogues.speaker: Kokuchuu
dialogues.text: Based on my studies of the ancient texts, hypersensitivity is usually treated with desensitization therapy. So, I figure there's no reason it shouldn't work in reverse.

dialogues.speaker: Kokuchuu
dialogues.text: Now, for a poor chap like yourself, with no sensitivity to spirits whatsoever, you'll have to completely immerse yourself in spiritually rich substances for this to be effective. I'm electing to name this approach "hypersensitization therapy"...

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: ...Is it risky?

dialogues.speaker: Kokuchuu
dialogues.text: You're the spirit-duffer, not me. I'm sure you're more clued up than I am on the potential consequences of brute-force clairvoyance. Ultimately, it's your decision.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Alright... But I do have one last question... What's in this for you?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: People like me obviously don't have much clout in this tribe, so it's not like I can offer you much in return.

dialogues.speaker: Kokuchuu
dialogues.text: You think I'm looking for a reward? Oh, my good sir! Take a look at my face. Isn't the answer written here, clear as day?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Uh... What? What's written there...?

dialogues.speaker: Kokuchuu
dialogues.text: "Just a friendly guy who's happy to help."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? So... some random guy from Inazuma just felt like helping Leyla cure his... spirit-duffer... ness?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hypersensitization therapy, huh... What a novel idea. Could that really work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not on Leyla, by the looks of things.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, it's anything but novel. Our tribe used to offer it as a treatment once upon a time, but it was so fraught with risks and had such an abysmal success rate that it was eventually outlawed.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: As for this Kokuchuu fellow... I'm sure he has his own agenda. He conveniently disappeared right after Leyla got into this mess.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Leyla's parents gave me the address of the camp, so I went and checked it out. There were clear traces of spiritual energy, and also... look what I found.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A broken shard... probably from a weapon or some sort of ceremonial implement.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You feel that? It might look old, but it has extremely strong traces of spiritual energy.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Leyla must have used this as his medium. It would definitely explain how a spirit-duffer like him was able to trigger a clairvoyant experience.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Wait, there's something else... It feels so familiar... I think this is somehow connected to my ancient name...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Connected how? Is it, like, a shard of an ancient name?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No... More like, I think this item might have belonged to a previous bearer of my ancient name.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps it was Sanhaj?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, that's it, Granny's getting itchy clairvoyance fingers. I'm going to try using this shard as a medium.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Cool, same as last time? {NICKNAME} can use the spiritloom to record what you find on a woven scroll.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Nope, Ororon can do the recording this time.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's a safety measure.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #You have a better understanding of the spirit domain than {NICKNAME}. If this really is a Sanhaj relic, you'll be better placed to deal with the fallout in the event that something goes wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Ah... See, Paimon? Told you Granny has a soft spot for {NICKNAME}. Look at her not wanting to put {M#him}{F#her} in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, I'm just a grandkid, so I'm expendable.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey! What are you blabbing on about?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Sorry, Granny. I'm ready now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Then let us begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! What's on the scroll this time... Looks like a broken bow, covered in flames...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't you think one of the pieces looks just like this shard?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right! It seems to be from the body of the bow...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I saw a bow just like this in one of Granny's scrolls...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Yes, it's the weapon Sanhaj used in the Battle of the Mare Jivari. I guess that proves it — this shard is a bona fide Sanhaj relic.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Good old Sanhaj... The relic's spiritual energy was fluctuating very strongly, but I wasn't in any danger at all. {NICKNAME} probably would have been fine as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that's a true hero, huh? Generations later, and the stuff he used to own is helping to treat spirit-duffers.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I still think there's more to this story, though. Kokuchuu must have had his own motives beyond just treating Leyla's condition.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, well... Okay, we saw the full bow just now, right? Maybe he wanted to see it too, so he could track down the other pieces?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I don't know if he'd have anything to gain by doing that. Even if they're Sanhaj relics, I still doubt he'd have much use for a broken bow.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Also, why use a spirit-duffer in that case? You're basically setting yourself up for failure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Leyla's body is responding!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let me take a look. I can sense a spirit being drawn to the relic...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Looks like Granny's plan is working. Leyla's spirit is being drawn to the bait.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In that case, let me try again — this time using both Leyla's body and the shard as mediums.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You can do it, Granny. I'm ready to go too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, can I control the spiritloom this time?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You got the itch too, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus Ororon went last time. It's only fair to take it in turns.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Fine by me. We know it's safe now, so you shouldn't have any problems.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, if you insist, be my guest. Just let me know when you're ready.

talks.objective: Use the spiritloom to weave the scroll
Use the spiritloom to weave the scroll

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm quite sure the shard is safe. There shouldn't be any danger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another image has appeared! This one is... a map!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: A map? Of where?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Could it be... the Mare Jivari?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Mare Jivari!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Mare Jivari was reduced to a desolate wasteland after that big battle. Or rather, it became known as the Mare Jivari after what happened there.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The ashes of the monsters and warriors who fought there covered the entire battlefield. Sometimes, bone-chilling cries would be heard from the depths. Other times, the whole region would become engulfed in towering flames, drowning out the cries...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That place is full of untold dangers and mysteries. Over the centuries, the finest adventurers have tried to prove themselves by venturing in... Sadly, most ended up perishing there.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That lasted up until around twenty or thirty years ago, when strange things started happening. People started speaking of an enormous, dark creature the size of a mountain roaming inside the Mare Jivari...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And then, shortly after that, the whole region just completely disappeared. Nobody knows how, but that infamously ominous place just vanished from the face of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!? How the heck!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know, right? Anyway, if I'm not mistaken, the place indicated on this map is where it used to be before it disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And where is that?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: At the westernmost part of Natlan. It's a very remote location, far away from any of the tribes. There never used to be a settlement there, but there's been more people since the Mare Jivari disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, that's just what I've heard. I've never been there myself.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is what age does to you. The older you get, the less adventurous you become.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's just an excuse. Granny's too lazy to take a trip that far away...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on a second! There's a spirit approaching the shard and the woven scroll!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Leyla's body is responding again!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Quite a strong reaction this time. Does this mean what he was really seeking was the Mare Jivari's location?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I sense it too... There's a soul nearby — almost a complete one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! This is creeping Paimon out...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Seems like the plan is working.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, um... can we just wake him up now?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Not today. You might think bringing a spirit back into its body is like pouring water from one bottle into another, but it's far more complicated than that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I need to borrow a ceremonial sword, and make some other preparations. It'll take me about two days.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But don't worry, now that his spirit's returned, there's just one step left. Let's meet up again in two days.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You ready?

choices.text: I need a little more time.
